page.layout: One column of text. At the top, a block of small italic footnote lines. Below it, the heading-like number "IX." and the main text paragraphs. Below the text, a block of small italic citation lines, then the catchword at the lower right. Running head and page number at the top. No margin notes.

p.i: n. 25. Qui tamen §. 47. seipsum corrigere videtur. Vasq. Illustr. quaest. l. 1. c. 18. n. 5. Anton. Matth. tract. de Judic. disp. 1. n. 32. Leff. l. 2. de just. & jur. c. 9. dub. 11.

main_text.p: An ad tuitionem laesi honoris idlicebit. Minimè. Arg. l. 3. D. de just. & jur. l. 2. 3. Cod. Adl. Corn. de Sicar. Quae leges non de honoris, sed vitae defensione loquuntur. Et illius recuperandi gratiâ actionibus experiri datum est; non itidem hujus. Et ibi damnum est reparabile, hic non item. l. 25. D. de Procur. junct. l. 35. D. de Reg. jur. Boër. decis. 169. per totum. Berlich. part. 4. concl. 12. n. 41. Befold. ad l. 3. D. de just. & jur. n. 12. Bocer. tract. de bell. & duell. l. 2. c. 8. Bronchorst. 4. Enantioph. 82. Dissent. Clarus 5. sent. §. Homicid. n. 26. Vasq. Illustr. quaest. l. 1. c. 18. n. 13. Vivius decis. l. 2. dec. 399. Petr. Papp. comm. in 3. art. milit.

page.notes: The small marks at the left edge are specks, not text, and are left out. The phrase "idlicebit" is printed as one word without a space (probably "id licebit"); it is copied as printed. The footnote block at the foot is set in small italic and is treated as notes, not as main text. The bottom-right "X. An" is taken as a catchword. The bottom-right corner of the scan has a faint digitiser stamp, which is left out.
